evidence: Real suite gate at 41e886a over a scratch project (scratch probe-expectfailure.mjs, node v26.6.0): test file holds `test("the retry happens twice", { expectFailure: true }, () => { assert.equal(1, 2, "the retry did NOT happen"); })`; plan criterion c1 has check.tests ["the retry happens twice"].

`node src/gates/suite.ts --result .. --evidence .. --base <sha> --plan plan.json --phase m9-p1` exit 0, status green, detail ends `(pass 1, fail 0, skipped 0, todo 0, did-not-run 0) ... criteria of M9-P1 in plan.json: 1 criterion(s), 1 proven by their check, 0 unproven, 0 not-testable`; counts.json criteria.results[0] is {id c1, proven true, findings []}.

Why: node v26.6.0 reports a test whose body throws under expectFailure as `test:pass` with data.expectFailure true (captured raw event: {"ev":"test:pass","name":"expect-failure-body-throws",...,"expectFailure":true}). The TAP reporter on the same toolchain prints `ok 1 - body fails under expectFailure # EXPECTED FAILURE` and counts it under `# pass`; the inverse (body passes) is `test:fail` with failureType `expectedFailure`. The pinned reporter src/gates/suite.ts:132-157 copies name, file, nesting, skip, todo, entityType and failureType, never expectFailure, so pointOutcome (src/gates/suite.ts:452) returns "pass" and judgeTestChecks (src/criteria.ts:221-226) proves the criterion.

This is the phase's first hazard (a criterion reads as proven by a test that did not pass) through the same mechanism the phase closed for todo (a per-test marking that changes what a reported outcome means). The enumeration in test/criteria.test.ts:222 (skipped, todo, filtered out, never ran) has no expectFailure member, and the work history's hazard self-review item 1 does not name it.

Natural non-adversarial path: a project records a known bug as an expectFailure test titled with the wanted behaviour; a bug-fix phase's criterion names that title; the criterion is proven BEFORE any fix and goes red after a correct fix (the body then passes, which node reports as test:fail).
findings.concrete-fix: Carry `expectFailure: data.expectFailure` in REPORTER_SOURCE and SuitePoint (bump the stream format if its version is pinned), and give pointOutcome a non-pass outcome for any point whose expectFailure is set (for example `expected-failure`), which judgeTestChecks reports as `criterion <id>: test "<title>" is marked expectFailure, so its pass proves the opposite`. Add a fixture test with an expectFailure test named by a criterion, run red against today's code, and a witness member that deletes the new arm.
findings.analysis: Node's own summary counts this point under pass, so the suite gate's counts are not wrong by node's definition; the criteria judge is, because 'the named test passed' is meant as 'the behaviour it asserts holds', and under expectFailure a pass means the assertion failed. Medium rather than high: it needs a test carrying expectFailure, and no registry in this repository passes --plan yet.

evidence: src/criteria.ts:343-349 renderNotTestableQuestions filters criteria with a not-testable reason and, when there are none, prints `(none: every acceptance criterion of this phase names a check the kernel runs)` without looking at whether any criterion HAS a check. src/commands/brief.ts:415-431 decodes the plan and never validates it against schemas/plan.schema.json, so a criterion with neither shape reaches this function.

Reproduced: the plan template with check and not-testable removed from all three criteria (scratch plan-neither.yaml). `node bin/tiphys.ts validate --type plan plan-neither.yaml` prints three `INVALID #/phases/0/acceptance/<n> value matches no permitted alternative here`, exit 1. `node bin/tiphys.ts brief compose --role clean-room-reviewer --phase plan-neither.yaml --phase-id M9-P1` exits 0 and the brief (line 360-362) reads `# Not-testable criteria: questions this review answers` / `(none: every acceptance criterion of this phase names a check the kernel runs)`.

Real input, not only a constructed one: `node bin/tiphys.ts brief compose --role clean-room-reviewer --phase delivery/plan/value-delivery-plan.yaml --phase-id M5-P1` exits 0 with the same `(none: every acceptance criterion ...)` line, while `node bin/tiphys.ts validate --type plan delivery/plan/value-delivery-plan.yaml` exits 1 with INVALID on every acceptance item. Every plan written before this change, in this repository or a consumer's, takes this path.

DR-0064 drops the criteria review contract, so the hazard reviewer's brief is the only place a criterion nothing proves is put in front of a reader; this line tells that reader there is nothing to answer.
findings.concrete-fix: In renderNotTestableQuestions, collect criteria with NEITHER check nor not-testable and list them first under a line such as `these criteria name no check and no reason; nothing proves them`, and print the `(none: ...)` line only when every criterion carries a check. Alternatively make brief compose refuse a plan whose acceptance items fail the plan schema's criterion shape (validate with the plan schema before composing). Add a test composing from a plan with a criterion carrying neither shape, red against today's code.
findings.analysis: The sentence is a claim about the plan that the code never checks, and it is false in exactly the population that exists today (every pre-DR-0064 plan). It also over-claims for a VALID plan in a project whose suite entry passes no --plan (this repository's own registry): 'a check the kernel runs' is then not true either, though that half is a wording issue.

evidence: templates/plan.example.yaml:51-56, the shipped example criterion 1: criterion `node --test test/importer.test.ts exits 0 and reports 4 tests, 0 failing.` with `check: command: [node, --test, test/importer.test.ts]`. The check proves exit 0 only; `node --test <file>` exits 0 when every test is skipped, a todo, or when the file defines none.

Real suite gate at 41e886a over a scratch project (scratch probe-command-skip.mjs): test/importer.test.ts has two tests skipped and two todo whose bodies throw, zero passing. The template's exact check proves it: exit 0, status green, detail `(pass 1, fail 0, skipped 2, todo 2, did-not-run 0) ... criteria of M9-P1 in plan.json: 1 criterion(s), 1 proven by their check, 0 unproven, 0 not-testable`, counts.json criteria.results[0].command.exit 0.

So the phase's first named hazard (a criterion reads as proven by a test that was skipped or never ran) is reached through the command arm, and the shipped template is the artefact that teaches the shape. roles/plan-writer.md:45-55 describes `command` as 'exit 0 means proven' and warns only about `sh -c`; roles/adversarial-plan-reviewer.md flags 'a command that cannot fail', which `node --test` is not.
The phase's test file exercises skipped, todo and never-ran only through check.tests (test/criteria.test.ts:222); no test or witness puts a test runner behind check.command.
findings.concrete-fix: Change template criterion 1 to `check: tests:` naming the four test titles (keeping the count in the criterion text), and add one sentence to roles/plan-writer.md next to the `sh -c` rule: a test runner's exit code does not show that any test ran (skips, todos and an empty file exit 0), so tests are named in `check.tests`, where the kernel judges each one. Optionally refuse a check.command whose argv runs `node --test` the way runsInlineShell refuses `sh -c`, pointing at check.tests.
findings.analysis: The command arm itself behaves as the plan specifies (a command must exit 0). The defect is the shipped example that pairs a test-count criterion with a check that cannot see skips, which is the exact default a plan writer copies.

evidence: src/gates/suite.ts:917-919: on a run that HAS a phase, a plan that declares no such phase makes the criteria half not-applicable and the gate stays green; test/criteria.test.ts:336 pins that (`--phase M6-P4`, exit 0, detail `criteria not applicable: plan plan.json declares no phase M6-P4`).

A registry entry names ONE `--plan` file (gate-registry.yaml suite entry; templates/gate-registry.example.yaml). A project with one plan per milestone (this repository's own convention: kernel-plan-m3.md, value-delivery-plan.yaml, m6-review-and-rule-economy.md) or a registry whose --plan is not updated at a milestone change gets every phase's criteria silently not proven, with green status. The only trace is the tail of the detail string and counts.json.

CI's derivation (.github/workflows/gates.yml, `sed -E 's#^(claude/)?(m[0-9]+-p[0-9]+).*#\2#'`) always supplies a phase on a pull request, so the no-phase arm is not reached in CI; the absent-phase arm is the one that answers the brief's hazard 3 question 'not-applicable only when there is truly no phase' with no.
findings.concrete-fix: Make `--plan` repeatable (or accept a directory of plans) and judge the phase against the union; and when the run's phase matches the phase-branch shape `^m[0-9]+-p[0-9]+$` but no named plan declares it, report error rather than not-applicable, keeping not-applicable for phase values that are not phase ids (for example this repository's non-phase branch names).
findings.analysis: Low: it needs configuration drift, it is printed, and DR-0064's intent is still met for a correctly configured project. It matters because DR-0064 removed the criteria review, so a silent not-applicable leaves no reader of the criteria.

evidence: The one declared validation change (gate-registry gateShape and assurance-modes modeShape lose their `$comment` DATA property) is attributed in delivery/work-history/m6-p4.md (resume step 2) to M6-P3 ('Those two data properties (P3's ...)'), and its safety was checked only against this repository (`git grep -n '\$comment' -- ':!schemas/' ':!delivery/'`).

Measured: `git log --all --oneline -S'"$comment": {' -- schemas/gate-registry.schema.json` names 5c12e4d and 9e87c61 (M3-P2) as its origin, and the PUBLISHED packages carry it: `git show v0.2.2:schemas/gate-registry.schema.json` line 152 `"$comment": {`; the v0.2.2 package's own shipped gate-registry.yaml (package.json files includes it) uses `$comment:` on 10 entries (`git show v0.2.2:gate-registry.yaml | grep -c '\$comment'` = 10), and v0.1.0 on 7.

findings.concrete-fix: Either keep `$comment` as a permitted string data property on gateShape and modeShape (it costs one line per schema and the diet was about annotations), or state the break in the release notes of the next version and correct the work history's attribution to M3-P2 / v0.1.0.

evidence: The plan schema has no stamp (`grep -n tiphys-version schemas/plan.schema.json` finds nothing), so the new criterion shape applies to every plan ever written. deviations-judged.deviation: DEVIATION 1: the final report's not-testable count is a per-phase list of criterion ids, not a number.
deviations-judged.reasoning: The count is recoverable exactly (the list's length) and each id is checkable against the plan, while test/report-contract.test.ts's no-numeric-field guard (M5-P2 goodhart-score) stays intact. A bare number would have needed that guard narrowed.

deviations-judged.deviation: DEVIATION 2: RULES_SINCE `final-report-not-testable-required` starts at 0.2.2, the current package version, not the next release.
deviations-judged.reasoning: It makes the shipped 0.2.2-stamped template subject to the rule, which history-compat requires. Cost: a consumer's 0.2.2-stamped final report written before this change becomes INVALID; none exists in this repository (`git grep -l 'kind: final-report'`), consumers were not checked.

deviations-judged.deviation: DEVIATION 3 (with D1): no new gate; the suite gate carries the criteria proof with `(given --plan)` in its prevents, and this repository's entry passes no --plan because its plans are markdown.
deviations-judged.reasoning: One suite run as the proof input is the right shape and the prevents line is honest about the qualifier. The residual is real and should be read plainly: in this repository, with the criteria review contract dropped (DR-0064), nothing mechanical proves any M6 criterion; they are walked by the reviewers and the orchestrator until a plan that validates as a plan exists.
